claims.text: An alert is a condition checked automatically that tells a person something needs attention; an incident is an unplanned loss or degradation of the service customers receive.
claims.source_hint: content/glossary.yaml alert, incident; Google SRE book, ch. Monitoring Distributed Systems (alerting on symptoms)

claims.text: Alert fatigue: alerts that need no action teach people to ignore alerts, until the alert that matters is ignored or read late too.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/alerts.md lines 15-16 at stage-4; Google SRE book, ch. Monitoring Distributed Systems

claims.text: An alert on a cause (CPU, a restarted Pod, a slow Redis) fires when customers notice nothing and stays silent when a cause nobody listed breaks the service, because no one can list every way a system breaks.

alerts.md: alerts call a person on what customers feel, SLIs S1-S4 of slo.md; any cause giving customers errors or slow answers (database, Redis, a release, a wrong setting) makes an SLI worse, so they catch unlisted causes; a cause not reaching customers leaves them quiet.

alerts.md sets no alert on CPU, memory or Pod restarts: they move while customers see nothing and alerts on them teach the person on duty to ignore alerts; the person receiving a symptom alert opens the dashboard to find why. Try it (b), (d): no alert.

slo.md: S1 = POST api/v1/orders (and v2) not 5xx, S2 = those answered fast enough, S3 = GET api/v1/products and api/v1/products/{id:int} not 5xx (503 of catalog-reads counts as bad), S4 = refund requests answered fast enough.

alerts.md gives each SLI two alerts: level page is meant to call the person on duty at once (on-call.md), level ticket is a task handled in working hours; ProductReadsFastBurn watches S3. At stage-4 nothing sends the call (alerts.md lines 83-85).

An SLI alert fires only when the bad share is above its threshold (in both windows) and stays so for the 'Giữ trong' time; thresholds come from how fast the error budget is spent, the 'burn' in names like ProductReadsFastBurn.
Each SLI's bad share adds up every api Pod Prometheus scrapes, api, api-canary and api-green (the green Deployment of the blue-green deployment), so a canary's requests count like the others.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/alerts.md lines 47-49; docs/design/slo.md lines 16-18 at stage-4; devops.l4.blue-green-deployment core concepts

claims.text: alerts.md plans three ticket-only cause alerts, none running: ready messages in any queue whose name ends in .dead for 10 minutes, a failed restore test, a failed db-backup or migration Job; reasons: staging scrapes only api Pods, restore test by hand, no object state collected.
A dead-lettered order message means the order was placed and answered with success, yet its email is not sent unless a person acts: nothing retries a dead-lettered message automatically.
claims.source_hint: backend.l3.dead-letter-queue five-line summary (line 5); backend.l3.queue-backlog-metrics summary line 5 (api 5xx stays 0)

claims.text: donhang-api.json has six panels: requests per second by status code, 5xx per second, p95 response time, orders placed per second, order emails waiting in RabbitMQ, dead-lettered order messages.
Grafana in the Compose profile monitoring loads donhang-api.json; staging's platform/monitoring holds only Prometheus (no Grafana), so the dashboard exists only in Compose at stage-4.
claims.source_hint: docker-compose.yml service grafana (profiles: [monitoring]); deploy/gitops/config-repo/platform/monitoring/prometheus.yaml lines 1-5 at stage-4

claims.text: Prometheus keeps an alert's state (pending, firing), visible in Prometheus, but sends no notification itself; staging runs no component that does, as alerts.md's last section records, so nobody is called at stage-4.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Alerting overview (Alertmanager sends notifications); docs/design/alerts.md lines 83-85 at stage-4

claims.text: S1 counts POST api/v1/orders and api/v2/orders not answered with 5xx; its fast alert (OrderPlacementFastBurn) has level page. Try it (c): the dead-letter row is a planned ticket, not running at stage-4.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/slo.md line 24; docs/design/alerts.md line 53 at stage-4

claims.text: CPU can be high while every request is answered in time (as under a load test) and normal while customers get errors; a dashboard shows a problem only to someone looking, an alert is checked all the time.
claims.source_hint: outline misconceptions 2-3; docs/design/alerts.md lines 15-18 at stage-4

claims.text: Trade-offs: cause alerts fire without harm and miss unlisted causes, fitting rarely since firing with nothing to do leads to alert fatigue; symptoms plus a few cause tickets suit when some failures (lost emails) hurt later than SLIs show; dashboards only need someone looking.
claims.source_hint: derived from docs/design/alerts.md lines 8-18, 67-79 at stage-4

claims.text: Choices: a service with no SLI yet → write its SLI first; a CPU alert meanwhile fires when nobody is hurt and teaches ignoring alerts; a disk filling while SLIs are fine → a ticket-level cause alert; an alert per 5xx → the SLI alert already counts every 5xx and fires on a share.
claims.source_hint: derived from docs/design/alerts.md lines 8-18, 67-70 at stage-4
